title: How to Stop Scam Calls and Texts on a Smartphone: Free Tools First, Then Paid Add-Ons
subtitle: Free tools are a good first step, and here is when a paid add-on may be worth considering.
excerpt: Your phone and your carrier offer free tools for scam calls and texts. Here is how they work, and what Verizon Call Filter Plus, AT&T ActiveArmor Advanced and Nomorobo Max add for a fee.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: The phone rings, and it is a number you don't know. Maybe it looks local. Maybe it is a text saying a package is stuck or an account is locked. Answer enough of these and you start dreading your own phone, which is a shame, because it is also how the doctor's office, the pharmacy and the grandkids reach you.

The good news is that you don't have to spend money to start cutting down on this. Your smartphone and your wireless carrier include free tools. Paid add-ons go further, but they are a second step, not the first.
How call and text filtering works

The Federal Trade Commission says call blocking and call labeling are the best defense. On a cell phone, a call-blocking app acts as a filter. Do Not Disturb works differently: it sends calls straight to voicemail.

Start with what is built in. According to AARP, an iPhone can silence unknown callers, so calls from numbers not saved in your contacts won't ring. iPhone spam detection also puts suspected spam in a separate section of the call log. On Android, AARP says to go to Block Numbers, then turn on Block Spam and Scam Calls. AARP also notes that a unique ringtone for your contacts helps you spot unknown callers.
For texts, AARP advises forwarding scam messages to 7726 (it spells SPAM) and not replying to unknown senders. Scammers spoof local numbers, so a familiar area code is no guarantee.
One thing that won't help much with scammers is the Do Not Call Registry. It only stops lawful sales calls. As the FTC puts it: "Being on the Registry won't stop scammers from making illegal calls."

items: Free first: Verizon's basic Call Filter is free on standard monthly and prepaid plans with a compatible phone (data usage applies). AT&T's page says spam text protection and other basic features are free in its app, so check exactly what is included before paying for more.
Ongoing cost: paid tiers renew automatically. $3.99 a month is about $48 a year, and $7 a month is $84 a year.

Features you will actually use: caller ID by name and a personal block list help with calls. Credit monitoring, VPN and similar extras go beyond scam calls, so you may not need them if call blocking is your goal.
Phone compatibility: older phones, basic flip phones and tablets may not be supported. Check the maker's page before signing up.
Easy pause or allow list: you want a simple way to make sure calls from the doctor, pharmacy or a contractor still get through.
How to cancel: Verizon says deleting its app does not turn filtering off, and you must unsubscribe or turn off the filter. Cancel through your account, not by deleting the app.

sections.content: Be aware that Verizon's Neighborhood Filter, which sends calls from your own area code and prefix to voicemail, can also block calls you want. The same goes for any area-code blocking. Also, Verizon says healthcare and public-service calls can't be blocked by category. Nomorobo's claims here come from the company's own page, and the page says it is supported by all carriers.
Setting it up and using it well

Before you turn on any filter, save the numbers that matter in your contacts: your doctors, pharmacy, bank, neighbors and family. Then check that the filter's allow list includes them, so their calls still come through.
Then make a habit of checking your voicemail and the spam or blocked-call list regularly. Verizon, for example, sends blocked spam to voicemail by default, so a real message may be waiting there.

If a parent would find phone settings tricky, an adult child can set it up for them. Turn on the built-in phone settings, sign into the carrier app, add key contacts, and show where the spam list lives.

No filter catches everything. Verizon says plainly: "Verizon doesn't guarantee that all spam calls will be detected." And filters don't stop a person from talking someone into acting. The safest rule is simple: never give a code or money to anyone who calls or texts you first. Hang up and call back on a number you already know.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: If you only use a landline, these phone tools won't apply, and a landline call blocker is the better route. For everyone with a smartphone, a sensible plan is to turn on the free tools first, and only pay for more if you decide the extra features are worth the recurring cost.

products.name: Verizon Call Filter and Call Filter Plus
products.price: Call Filter free on standard monthly and prepaid plans with a compatible phone (data usage applies); Call Filter Plus $3.99/month; multi-line $10.99/month for 3 or more lines (November 2026)
products.blurb: For Verizon customers with Android 10 or later, or iOS 16.6 or later: the free version offers spam detection, a spam filter and an allow list, while Plus adds caller ID, spam lookup, a personal block list and blocking by category such as telemarketers or political calls. Not available on tablets or data-only devices.

products.name: AT&T ActiveArmor Advanced
products.blurb: For AT&T customers who want caller ID by name and location plus reverse number lookup, bundled with extras like credit and dark-web monitoring and identity-theft insurance. AT&T's page says basic features are free in the app, so check what is included before paying; if you only want call blocking, you may not need the extras.

products.name: Nomorobo Max (AARP member pricing)
products.price: $35.99/year for AARP members (regular $59.99); Max Family for up to 4 devices $47.99/year (regular $79.99) (November 2026)
products.blurb: For AARP members who want call screening, live voicemail transcription and spam text filtering, with a pause option while waiting for a doctor's or contractor's call. AARP membership is $15 for the first year and renews automatically.
